incidents.industry: Cross-sector (telecom, government, healthcare, finance, critical infrastructure)
incidents.vector: Large-scale credential stuffing, reuse and password spraying against exposed Fortinet management and VPN interfaces, using previously leaked credentials and a self-sustaining automated scanner.
incidents.impact: Attackers compiled verified working credentials for 30,791 internet-facing Fortinet devices across 194 countries; targeting was heavily weighted toward NATO members and included a defense-industry VPN endpoint. SOCRadar found the exposed operator server; the campaign remains active.

incidents.victim: Software supply chain (npm/PyPI/RubyGems) — incl. Red Hat, GitHub, European Commission, Mercor, LiteLLM
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — data and credential theft
incidents.vector: Self-propagating 'Shai-Hulud' worm spreading via compromised maintainer credentials and tokens across open-source package registries; abuses forgeable Git commit timestamps and author metadata to evade detection.
incidents.impact: Researchers confirmed 516 live malicious packages across five ecosystems, 3,000+ affected GitHub repositories and 200+ compromised developer accounts; 1,729 throwaway credential-theft repos and 151 active payload repos remained live as of Jun 16. GitHub dismissed two formal vulnerability reports on the enabling design flaws.

incidents.vector: Takeover of the 'ehindero' npm maintainer account to publish 140+ poisoned package versions injected with 'easy-day-js', a typosquat of dayjs whose postinstall hook ran an obfuscated dropper, disabled TLS verification, and fetched a second-stage tasking implant from C2.
incidents.impact: Any developer workstation or CI/CD pipeline running npm install/update after the compromise was exposed, risking credentials, tokens and build environments. Microsoft Threat Intelligence reported it to npm; packages were removed and publish access revoked.

incidents.victim: Oracle PeopleSoft customers (Council of Europe, Ralph Lauren, JCPenney, Nexstar, U. of Nottingham)
incidents.vector: Exploitation of an Oracle PeopleSoft zero-day (CVE-2026-35273, added to CISA KEV Jun 12) to steal large volumes of records, followed by extortion demands.
incidents.impact: The ShinyHunters group listed multiple victims on its leak site; University of Nottingham confirmed 40GB and the data of 450,000+ students and alumni stolen. Several listed organizations have confirmed breaches.

incidents.vector: State actors 'prepositioning' within technology underpinning critical national infrastructure to establish footholds for potential future disruption, exemplified by the China-linked Volt Typhoon tactic cited by the NCSC.
incidents.impact: NCSC chief Richard Horne disclosed his agency handled 200+ incidents affecting critical infrastructure in the year to May, about 75% attributed to hostile states; he warned adversaries are establishing footholds that could enable mass disruption in a future conflict.

incidents.victim: Healthcare and high-pressure sectors (INC ransomware victims)
incidents.vector: Double-extortion ransomware-as-a-service; intrusion via spearphishing, broker-supplied valid credentials, and exploitation of known flaws (Citrix Bleed 2, SimpleHelp, Citrix NetScaler, Fortinet EMS), with Rust-rewritten Windows/ESXi lockers.
incidents.impact: Acronis reports INC has claimed 800+ victims since 2023 and is among the most active RaaS gangs, repeatedly hitting healthcare orgs such as NHS Dumfries & Galloway and Alder Hey Children's Hospital; 124 incidents in Q1 2026 alone.

incidents.vector: Malspam and fake download/app sites delivering the Silver Fox (Winos) trojan, used to drop infostealers and custom AtlasRAT/ValleyRAT remote access trojans.
incidents.impact: Chinese police arrested 67 suspects across five provinces, including the malware author Ji Moufei; the group primarily targeted Chinese-speaking users to steal online assets and funds before recently expanding abroad.

incidents.victim: Web users via compromised WordPress sites (Lorem Ipsum campaign)
incidents.vector: After Microsoft disrupted the Fox Tempest signing service, operators abandoned Trojanized Teams installers for ClickFix lures on compromised WordPress sites, tricking users into pasting a PowerShell command that installs a multistage loader and backdoor.
incidents.impact: BlueVoyant links the Lorem Ipsum loader to the financially motivated group Rapid Brigantine (aka Vice Society/Vanilla Tempest), tied to Rhysida, BlackCat, Zeppelin and Quantum Locker ransomware, broadening the victim pool and raising the threat profile.

incidents.vector: Unauthorized access to parts of the company's internal network; specifics undisclosed.
incidents.impact: The Danish pharmaceutical giant (maker of Ozempic and Wegovy) took systems offline to evict attackers and confirmed some sensitive data, including patient PII, was copied.

incidents.vector: Attacker abused the AUR 'adopt orphaned package' mechanism to take over 1,900+ abandoned community packages and inject install procedures that pulled a malicious npm package (later a Bun script) deploying a rootkit and credential-harvesting infostealer.
incidents.impact: Massive weekend supply chain attack against the unofficial Arch Linux repository; the infostealer collects browser, Electron-app and developer secrets. Affected users urged to rotate all credentials and remove persistence. Hijack attempts were ongoing at time of reporting.

incidents.victim: 1.2M websites via Awesome Motive WordPress plugins
incidents.vector: Malicious code added to legitimate JavaScript of three Awesome Motive plugins (OptinMonster, TrustPulse, PushEngage); it waits for an admin login, creates a rogue admin account, and installs a self-hiding backdoor plugin.
incidents.impact: More than 1.2 million websites were backdoored following a security incident at the major WordPress plugin developer, per Sansec.

incidents.victim: Iranian banks (Bank Melli, Tejarat, Saderat, Export Development Bank)
incidents.vector: Attack reportedly targeted communications infrastructure shared by the four banks, disrupting online portals and mobile apps.
incidents.impact: A cyberattack disrupted services at four of Iran's largest banks over the weekend amid the ongoing Iran War. Iran's banking council said no customer data was accessed.

incidents.vector: Compromise of the lawmaker's Signal messaging account; method undisclosed.
incidents.impact: The FBI notified the Nebraska Republican — a staunch Ukraine supporter and Kremlin critic — that suspected Russian hackers had breached his Signal account.

incidents.vector: Data allegedly stolen from a government agency managing healthcare entitlements; intrusion method undisclosed.
incidents.impact: Hackers allegedly stole personal information on more than 67 million Thai citizens, with some of the data posted on online black markets. The Thai government launched an investigation.

incidents.vector: Terabytes of data taken in April from an unsecured database exposed online; leaked after ransom negotiations failed.
incidents.impact: The FulcrumSec group claims it obtained passport details for children and parents, attendance records, teacher passwords and visitor photos from the K-12 operator, then leaked the data after a failed extortion negotiation.

incidents.vector: Cyberattack of undisclosed type that halted operational systems.
incidents.impact: Australia's second-largest sugar producer paused cane haulage and milling at two Mackay-region mills at the start of the annual crushing season.

incidents.vector: Ransomware-as-a-service offering a 90/10 affiliate split; gains entry via internet-facing devices (VPNs, firewalls) and encrypts entire networks within hours.
incidents.impact: Check Point ranks the group the second-most-active ransomware gang of 2026 with 332+ published victims since mid-2025. Krebs traced the administrator (Hastalamuerte/Zeta88) to an individual in Izhevsk, Russia.

incidents.victim: Check Point Security Gateway / VPN users
incidents.vector: Active exploitation of a Check Point Security Gateway improper-authentication flaw (CVE-2026-50751, added to CISA KEV Jun 8) affecting remote-access tools, firewalls and VPNs.
incidents.impact: CISA gave federal agencies three days to patch the VPN bug reported as under attack by the Qilin ransomware operation; Check Point confirmed several remote-access products are affected.

incidents.vector: Spear-phishing campaign luring WhatsApp users to click a malicious link leading to an external site, in violation of a 2024 U.S. court injunction barring NSO from targeting the platform.
incidents.impact: Meta says it detected and disrupted the new NSO campaign and filed a contempt complaint; it urged U.S. lawmakers to maintain sanctions on the sanctioned, Entity-Listed spyware maker.

incidents.vector: Active exploitation of a PAN-OS authentication-bypass flaw (CVE-2026-0257) in the GlobalProtect portal and gateway, allowing attackers to circumvent controls and initiate VPN connections.
incidents.impact: Unit 42 observed an unidentified actor exploiting the CISA KEV-listed flaw; only a small portion of probed devices established VPN sessions and no post-access lateral movement was confirmed at time of reporting.
